area: Git governance / sealed commit bundle deletion attribution
finding: TASK-GIT-0029 sealed commit attribution protects add/modify content, but staged deletions are not represented in the sealed bundle because `ls-files -s` has no entry for a staged deletion. An in-scope deleted file can therefore survive in the committed tree instead of being delivered as an intentional deletion.
expectedBehavior: Sealed commit bundles must represent deletion as an explicit tombstone and compare the committed tree against that tombstone. Commit assembly must remove tombstoned paths from the candidate index without re-adding worktree content, and any missing, extra, or wrong-blob result must fail closed before ref mutation.
evidenceOrRepro: Claude-006 closeout report for TASK-GIT-0029: delete `src/gone.txt` and modify `src/stay.txt` through sealed commit; the resulting HEAD keeps `gone.txt`. Captain verification also observed staged deletions for `release/atm-root-drop/packages/core/dist/skills/incident-learning-candidate.d.ts` and `release/atm-root-drop/packages/core/dist/skills/index.d.ts` after TASK-GIT-0029 close.
followUp: TASK-GIT-0030 Represent deletions in sealed commit bundles. Do not emergency-reopen TASK-GIT-0029 unless owner separately authorizes anomaly repair; keep normal delivery on queue/wait/CAS and no override lease.
